text.p: An earthquake measuring 4.8 on the Richter scale hit the cities of Ardabil and Nir in northwestern Iran on Monday, two days after a massive quake devastated the country's eastern region, the official news agency IRNA said.
There was no report yet on possible loss of life or damage to property in the latest quake, which struck at 8:20 a.m. (0350 GMT).
The agency said the seismological base of Tabriz in east Azarbaijan province registered the epicentre at Sar'ein region 25 km (15 miles) west of Ardabil.
Many tremors with magnitude of more than four have hit Ardabil since February 28 when an earthquake with an intensity of 5.5 jolted the region, killing about 1,000 people and injuring at least 2,600.
About 2,400 people were killed and 6,000 injured in Saturday's quake in eastern Iran.
